To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the c-Myc transgene in cMyc-CHO-K1 cells has a significant effect on the proteome and the proteins involved in proliferation, adhesion and protein biosynthesis.
the c-Myc gene is involved in the regulation of a number of proteins that are involved in cell adhesion, cell cycle and energy metabolism.

cMycCHO cell lines have increased protein expression of nucleolin, eIF6, ATP synthase and vimentin, while the expression of proteins involved in matrix and adhesion are decreased, which could explain why the cMycCHO lines are easier to adapt to suspension.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the proteins involved in the cMyc phenotype and the pathways that are activated in cMyc over-expressed CHO cells.
the identification of differentially expressed proteins in cMyc over-expressing cells, which may be responsible for the increased proliferation rate and integral viable cell number observed.
the proteome of cMycCHO and the proteins that are differentially expressed compared to the parental cell line.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
c-Myc has a positive effect on CHO cell proliferation and protein expression.

the cMycCHO cell line exhibits a higher integral viable number due to a higher proliferation rate and a lower cell death rate, and that this is due to a change in the expression of proteins involved in proliferation, adhesion, and metabolism.

c-myc is a transcription factor that regulates a large number of genes, which in turn regulate the expression of a large number of other genes, which in the end, regulate cell proliferation, cell cycle progression, apoptosis and cell death.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
c-myc over-expressing CHO cell lines have an increase in protein biosynthesis, energy metabolism, and cell division and a decrease in cell adhesion.
cMycCHO has an increased number of proteins involved in proliferation, but a decreased number of adhesion related proteins.
cMycCHO cell lines have an altered proteome that is consistent with a higher proliferation rate and lower cell death rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cMycCHO has a greater number of proteins involved in proliferation, which is consistent with the higher integral viable cell numbers in cMycCHOs.
cMyc is a good choice to improve CHO cell proliferation and integral viable cell number, and the proteins identified here may help to explain why.
the cMycCHO cell line has a more active protein biosynthesis and metabolism than the wild type CHO cell line.
